item.title: OpenHoop 0.8.4
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.8.4

  • Run connectors. An object's Finish now has Then: Jump or Run. Run sews running stitches straight to the next part, which sews over them: no trim, no ties, and no thread left lying across the fabric, handy on machines without a thread cutter. A run only sews when the next part is the same thread with no stop in between (otherwise it jumps), and long runs get a warning.
  • Ties when you want them. Tie off and Tie in are now Off, Always or When far (only after a move of at least the tie distance, or where the thread is cut).
  • Connectors for the whole design. With nothing selected, Connectors in Properties sets the trim and tie distances, the tie stitches (how many and how long) and the run connector's stitch length.
  • Between letters. Lettering can trim when far (the font's own trims), always trim, jump without trimming, or run from letter to letter.

Designs that don't use these sew exactly as before. Designs that do need OpenHoop 0.8.4 or later to open.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.10
item.description:

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.9
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.9

  • Auto-digitize traces detailed pictures instead of giving up. A traced part with more points or holes than one fill can hold used to stop the whole trace; now tiny holes (smaller than the smallest part you keep) are filled in, only the 100 largest holes stay, and outlines are smoothed just enough to fit. The result says how many holes were filled in.
  • Very large designs always reopen. When the stitches a project stores to open quickly would make the file too big to open, they're left out and worked out again when it opens. A design too big even without them is refused when you save, with the reason, instead of being saved as a file that won't open.
  • Saving hoopings names an empty hooping ("Hooping 2 has nothing to sew…") and what to do about it, instead of failing with "There are no stitches to export".
  • Saving hoopings asks before replacing files. If hooping files or a hooping sheet with the same names are already in the folder, OpenHoop asks before replacing them.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.8
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.8

Getting started

  • OpenHoop asks which machine you sew on the first time it opens: the brand, the hoop new designs should start in, and whether the machine cuts the thread between parts. New designs then start in that hoop and exports in your machine's format (PES, JEF or VP3). If it doesn't cut threads, exporting reminds you about Stop at Jumps. Help › Set Up Your Machine… asks again any time. If you already use OpenHoop, your settings stay as they are.
  • A Help menu: the user guide (⌘?), Getting started, Report a Problem… (a short form on GitHub) and the website.
  • The user guide starts with a first sew-out, step by step, with which file format each machine brand needs, a section on Stop at Jumps, and a table of what to try when something sews wrong.

Fixes

  • Deleting a point after undoing the edit that added it no longer crashes.
  • A very small hoop (under 32 mm) with Multi-hooping no longer crashes or freezes; Auto layout explains why it can't lay out hoopings, as it does for a layout that would need more than 50.
  • An edit that would make a design too big to save (a shape with more than 2,000 points after a weld, say) is refused, and the status line says why. Before, the design couldn't be saved afterwards.
  • Stitches longer than 12 mm no longer make DST, EXP, JEF and XXX exports fail: they're split to fit the format, as the warning always said.
  • Exporting or printing a multi-hooped design no longer freezes OpenHoop while the hoopings are worked out.

The app now carries its own license text (GPL-3.0).

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.7
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.7

  • Smart corners for satin lines, satin outlines and satin borders. A corner sharper than 75° gets a mitre: a sharp point with a seam from the inside corner out to the tip, each side's stitches square to its own side and overlapping 0.5 mm across the seam, so no gap shows.
  • Caps for very sharp corners. Below 45°, the sides stop at a line across the corner and the point is sewn as a small piece of its own, its stitches running across the corner. The needle runs out to the point first, hidden under the cap. A cap whose stitches would be longer than 8 mm becomes a mitre.
  • Sharp points that used to be refused now sew, such as a 4 mm satin line with a 30° corner, or a border around a star.
  • On for new satin lines, outlines and borders. Untick Smart corners in Properties (under Width) to round the corners instead; tick it again to bring them back. Corners of 75° or more stay rounded.
  • Older designs keep their rounded corners and sew exactly as before. Designs with a smart corner are saved as a newer file version, so older versions of OpenHoop won't open them.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.6
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.6

  • Wreath / Kaleidoscope (⌥⇧W). Select something to repeat, such as a leaf, a flower or a word, and click a center. Dashed outlines preview the copies going all the way round. Set Copies (2–100) in Properties and tick Mirror every other for a kaleidoscope, where neighbouring copies face each other in pairs. Apply makes it as one step to undo.
  • Wreaths sew color by color. The wreath is one group, sewn one thread color at a time all the way round, so it changes thread no more often than the original selection did, however many copies it has.
  • Lettering envelopes. Bend straight lettering into a Bridge (curved top and bottom), Pennant (tapering), Perspective (leaning) or Diamond (to a point) shape. Pick one under Envelope in Properties, then type the handle moves or drag the handles with Edit Nodes (H). Shift bends the opposite handle the other way, and ⌘ bends it the same way.
  • Envelopes stay with the lettering. Change the text, font or size and the new letters are bent the same way. Projects with an envelope are saved as a newer file version, so older versions of OpenHoop won't open them.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.5
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.5

  • Underlay 1 and Underlay 2, each with its own settings. Satins and fills now have two underlay sections in Properties. Each has its own type and shows only the settings that type uses: Inset, Spacing, Length (new: the underlay's stitch length) and, for tatami, Angle.
  • Fills get two underlay layers. Each can be an inset edge run or tatami (sparse rows across the shape, now a type of its own). New fills sew an edge run, then tatami rows, the same stitches as the old "Edge + sparse". A tatami underlay's angle is measured from the fill's angle, so 90° runs straight across the top rows.
  • Crossed tatami. Pick Tatami for both layers and Underlay 2 starts square to Underlay 1: a crosshatch for big fills or stretchy fabric.
  • Double zigzag underlay for satins. A zigzag down the column and back, crossing itself in X's, for wide satins.
  • Older designs sew exactly as before. They open with their underlay split into the two layers. Designs that use the new options are saved as a newer file version, so older versions of OpenHoop won't open them.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.4
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.4

  • Review Sewing Order warns about moves worth a second look. While reviewing (⌥⇧R), two kinds of move turn terracotta:
  • Long moves: the next start is 15 mm or more from where the step before ended, in the same thread. That means time spent travelling, and a long tail to snip.
  • Untrimmed jumps: a jump isn't trimmed although it's at least the design's trim distance, so the thread lies across the fabric.

You'll see them on the canvas, in the step's details (with what you could do about it), as a small triangle on the step's row in Sewing order, and in a list under Route: click one to look at its step. Moves where the thread changes are never warned about, since the machine stops and starts afresh there anyway.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.3
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.3

  • See the whole sewing route. In Review Sewing Order (⌥⇧R), switch the Review section in Properties from Step to Route. Every step's number sits at its start, and an arrow runs from each step's end to where the next one starts: dashed for a trim, dotted for a thread change, a thin line for a jump that isn't trimmed. Numbers that would cover each other move aside, with a short line back to their start. Route also counts the trims and thread changes. Pressing ← → goes back to stepping.
  • Clearer travel lines in dark mode. The line from one step to the next no longer looks solid on dark fabric.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.2
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.2

  • Review Sewing Order (⌥⇧R). Step through a design in the order it sews, to check each object's start and end before you sew it. ← → step (also ↑ ↓ and ⌘T ⇧T), and clicking an object or a Sewing order row jumps to it. The canvas shows what's sewn so far with the step's start (+) and end (×), and a dashed line from where the step before ended, labelled with what happens on the way: *Trim, then 18.6 mm*, *Jump of 6.0 mm, not trimmed*, *Trim and thread change…*. A Review section at the top of Properties says the same, with Set… buttons, and the + and × can be dragged to move them. What's still to sew is faded, or hidden with Settings › Look › Reviewing the sewing order. The button is at the end of the tool strip's View group. Esc finishes.
  • Thread View shines. Stitches catch the light from the top left, so they look brighter or darker by which way they run, like thread under a lamp. Satins and fills now show their direction at a glance.
  • Step the stitch player from the keyboard. With nothing selected, ← → step one stitch and ↑ ↓ ten. PgUp / PgDn go to the previous or next color, ⇧T / ⌘T the previous or next object, ⌥← / ⌥→ the previous or next trim, and End the end of the design. They're in the View menu too.
  • More default keys, matching common embroidery software:
  • ⇧⌘E Remove Overlaps (Export Machine File keeps ⌘E and ⇧E), ⇧⌘X Clear Guides, ⌘[ / ⌘] Sew Earlier / Later, ⌥⌘← / ⌥⌘→ rotate 90°, ⇧⌘H show or hide the object.
  • ⇧L Sewing order panel, ⌥P Design panel, and ⌥⌘1–4 Sewing order, Design, Reference image and Threads.
  • Space finishes a shape while drawing, as Return does.
  • Keys you set yourself stay as they are.

Import a reference image with File › Import Reference Image… (⌘I) or the tool strip's Move & Size Artwork button, which imports one while the design has none. To keep the button, add it back with Customize Toolbar… (right-click the toolbar).

item.title: OpenHoop 0.7.0
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.7.0

  • One layout: the Guided view is gone. OpenHoop now always uses the layout that was called Pro: every tool is its own button in two rows across the top (or down the left side, in Settings › Tools & player), with a precision bar for exact position, size and rotation, the sewing order as a table with stitch counts, and live stats in the status bar.
  • If you used Guided, OpenHoop opens in this layout with its standard panel arrangement. If you used Pro, your panel arrangement is kept.
  • The Guided | Pro switch in the toolbar and View › Pro View (⌥⌘P) are gone; ⌥⌘P is free for a shortcut of your own.
  • Rest the pointer on any tool, button or setting to see what it does. These tooltips replace the lines of explanation Guided showed under each setting.
  • Nothing else changes: every tool and setting is still here, and projects open as before.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.9
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. It's in active development, and its designs have been sewn on a Brother SE600. Test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.9

  • Multi-hooping. Sew a design bigger than your hoop in several hoopings, re-hooping the fabric between them. Tick Multi-hooping under Sewing area in the Design panel and OpenHoop places enough hoopings to cover the design.
  • Each hooping shows on the canvas as a dashed outline in its own color, with its number. The new Hoopings tool (⌥⇧H) drags them.
  • Properties lists the hoopings in sewing order, with what each one sews. Click one to fade the others. Add more beside it, lay them out again automatically, or remove one.
  • Each object sews in the first hooping that holds all of it. A letter's parts always stay together, so a word can cross hoopings but a letter can't. Anything that fits no hooping is outlined in red until you fix it.
  • Alignment marks (a box with an X, or a cross) are sewn where hoopings overlap. The next hooping sews the same marks first and then stops, so you can check the fabric is lined up before it sews on.
  • Save Hoopings for Machine… saves one file per hooping (*Towel – hooping 1 of 3.pes*) and a printable hooping sheet with each hooping's threads and how to re-hoop for it.
  • Try your first multi-hooped design on scrap fabric to get a feel for lining up the marks. Multi-hooped projects are saved as a new file version that 0.6.8 and earlier can't open.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.8
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.8

  • New start and end markers. A selected object now shows where it starts as a green crosshair (+) and where it ends as a red crosshair turned to a cross (×), in place of the play and stop buttons. The middle is open, so you can see the exact stitch each one marks. Drag them just as before.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.7
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.7

  • Outlines & Offsets (⇧⌘O). Select fills or closed outlines and choose Digitize › Add › Outlines & Offsets… to add new outlines around them: one right on the edge, and up to two offsets a set distance outside the shape (or inside it, with a distance below 0). Pick any line stitch, sharp or rounded corners, and whether to outline holes too. The dialog previews the result. Add Satin Border no longer has a default key; give it one in Settings if you like. A key you set for it yourself stays.
  • Remove Overlaps. Digitize › Pick & Shape › Remove Overlaps makes fills leave out the parts that shapes sewn on top of them cover, so they aren't stitched twice. It works on the selection, or the whole design with nothing selected. Nothing is cut for good: move the shape on top and the fill fills back in, and choosing it again sews the fills in full.
  • Keep drawing a finished line or satin. Select a running line or satin column, pick its drawing tool and click one of its ends to carry on drawing from there. Press Return to finish; it's one step to undo.
  • Satins as wide as you like. Satin columns, satin lines and satin borders are no longer capped. Where satin stitches come out longer than 12 mm, a warning suggests turning on Split wide satin, since stitches that long can snag.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.6
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.6

  • New shapes start without an outline. Picking Closed Shape, Freehand shape, Rectangle, Ellipse or Basic Shapes sets the next shape's Outline to None, instead of reusing the last outline you chose. Pick an outline and it applies to the shapes you draw with that tool until you pick a tool again. Your fill and other shape choices are still remembered.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.5
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.5

  • One export, any format. File › Export Machine File… (⌘E or ⇧E) replaces the separate Export PES…, DST…, EXP…, JEF…, VP3…, XXX… and PEC… items. Pick the format from the Format menu at the bottom of the save window: PES 6 (the default, for Brother and Baby Lock), PES 1, PEC, DST, EXP, JEF, VP3 or XXX. The file name follows your pick, and OpenHoop remembers the format you used last. Export Thread List… uses the same menu. Your ⌘E shortcut moves to the new item by itself.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.4
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.4

  • Properties follows the tool you pick. Choose a shape tool (Open or Closed Shape, Freehand, Rectangle, Ellipse or Basic Shapes) and Properties shows its Next shape settings straight away, even while something is selected. The selection stays put. Draw the shape and Properties shows the new shape; pick the tool again to get its settings back.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.3
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.3

  • Stop at Jumps, for machines without a thread cutter. A single-needle machine ignores trims and drags the thread across to the next part. Click Stop at Jumps in the Threads panel and the machine pauses after each jump, as it does for a thread change, so you can snip the loose thread and press Start to carry on. Your thread colors stay as they are. It works on the selected objects, or the whole design when nothing is selected. Click Remove Jump Stops to take them off again; stops you set yourself, such as appliqué's, stay.
  • The stitch player can pause where the machine would. Light the new scissors button beside Play, and playing stops at each trim, stop and thread change. Press Play to carry on to the next one.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.2
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.2

  • See a line stitch before you pick it. Line style in Properties is a button with a picture, like Fill style: click it for every style with a picture of its stitches, and point at one to see your line sewn that way on the canvas.
  • Next shape shows pictures too. Its Stitch, Fill and Outline buttons list each choice with a picture of its stitches, in the thread your next shape gets.
  • Names follow the stitch. A line called "Zigzag 2" becomes "Ripple 2" when you change its style. Names you've typed yourself stay as they are.
  • Stitch angle lines that can't be joined up are refused. When three or more lines meet the same part of a fill (a line in each point of a star, or each arm of a Y), the stitches can't turn from one to the next. The line isn't added, and the status line says why. A design that already has such lines shows the fill in red until some are moved or deleted.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.1
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.1

  • Updates come to you. OpenHoop now looks for new versions once a day while it's open, and OpenHoop › Check for Updates… looks right away. When there's one, it shows what's new and Install Update downloads it, installs it and reopens OpenHoop. Only updates signed by OpenHoop's maker are installed, and nothing about you or your designs is sent.
  • Settings › Updates turns the daily check off, or checks now.

This is the last version you need to download by hand: from here on, updates arrive inside the app.

item.title: OpenHoop 0.6.0
item.description:
OpenHoop is a free, open-source embroidery digitizing app for the Mac. This is an early preview: expect rough edges, and test-sew designs before stitching anything important.

New in 0.6.0

Fills

  • See a fill before you pick it. The Fill style button shows a picture of each style's stitches, and pointing at one shows your selected shape stitched that way on the canvas.
  • 26 tatami patterns. Zigzags, waves, herringbone, chevrons, blocks, steps, ribs and more, made by where each row's needle holes go. Pick from pictures; Smooth (the default) sews as before.
  • New fill styles: stipple, motif, cross stitch, gradient, guided (rows that bend along a line you draw) and satin fills.
  • Turning fills. Stitch angle lines bend tatami and satin fills round curves, in one smooth sweep, finishing at the end point you set.
  • Tatami row spacing is measured across two rows, as embroidery software usually does (0.40 mm lays rows 0.20 mm apart). Older designs open with their spacing converted, so they sew the same.
  • Straight fills with notches or holes hide their travel under rows sewn later.

Lines and satins

  • Line styles: zigzag, blanket, back stitch, stem stitch, motif runs and ripple.
  • Raised satin, and satins and lines that start or end part way along.
  • Borders, outlines and lines start and end right at their points.

Lettering

  • Lettering is one object, added and edited in Properties, with a font list you can arrow through and letters you can nudge.
  • Lettering can sit along a line you draw.

Threads

  • The Threads panel shows a whole thread chart: 21 brand charts and machine palettes, with search by name or number.
  • Each design keeps its own thread palette, under the canvas or docked in the Threads panel.

Working with objects

  • Drag rows in the sewing order to reorder them, and Sequence by Color.
  • Lock, rename and hide from the sewing order: click a row's lock, or right-click it.
  • Box-select with Select, resize handles on the selection, and a green start / red end marker you can drag.
  • With nothing selected, Properties shows the whole design: its size, stitch count, whether it fits the hoop, and its settings.
  • Corner and smooth points, Delete removes just the selected point, and test swatches with a density map.

Everything else

  • Millimeters or inches, rulers that mark the pointer, and a choice of light, dark or match-the-Mac.
  • Settings is a sidebar of short pages, including what new designs and objects start with.
  • Move & Size Artwork imports an image when the design has none.
  • Saved projects show their design as their Finder icon, and the window reopens at the size it was closed at.
  • Many speed-ups and fixes.

Note: designs that use the new stitch types are saved in a newer file version, so OpenHoop 0.5.0 can't open them.
